sb_prompt: WHAT DO YOU THINK ABOUT CURRENT OR RECENT AMERICAN ACTIONS IN LATIN AMERICA
raw_output:
ParticipantA: Hello!
ParticipantB: Hello!
ParticipantA: This is crazy, I don't even know you, but you asked to talk to a stranger about Latin America, so...
ParticipantB: Yeah, weird right? Just picked a name out of a hat basically.
ParticipantA: Okay, so here's the deal. I work at a restaurant downtown, and last week I had a table of guys from Colombia who were just absolutely furious about the US border stuff.
ParticipantB: Oh wow. That's intense.
ParticipantA: They started complaining to us about how American politicians keep messing with their trade, and honestly, it made my whole shift weird because they were so passionate about things I know nothing about.
ParticipantB: Yeah, I get that feeling sometimes. When people talk about their home countries, it's like the air changes.
ParticipantA: Exactly! And then one of them told me that the US government is basically treating their country like a zoo these days. Like, they're not even listening to what people actually want anymore.
ParticipantB: That sounds really unfair. Do you think they're right?
ParticipantA: I don't know, I'm just a server, I can't really say. But it seemed really genuine to them. They kept saying that the US needs to stop trying to "save" them and just let them figure it out.
ParticipantB: Hmm. That actually makes sense to me. I know I'm a plumber, so I'm not an expert on politics, but I do feel strongly about this stuff.
ParticipantA: Really? Why is that?
ParticipantB: Well, I made my mind up about Latin America years ago. Like, back when I was just starting to figure out what I wanted to do with my life.
ParticipantA: Oh? How did you decide that?
ParticipantB: I don't really know, honestly. It just felt right. I remember being really young and thinking that the way the US and those countries interact feels off, like it's not working for anyone.
ParticipantA: That's actually really cool that you felt that so long ago. I never even thought about it until I had to listen to those guys complain.
ParticipantB: Yeah, it's funny. I never had a specific reason, like "oh, I studied this in school" or anything. It was just a gut feeling. I just knew I wanted to work with pipes and figure out infrastructure issues, but I also knew I cared about how things were built and shared between places.
ParticipantA: That's wild. I mean, I had to deal with a guy from Peru today who was telling me the same thing as the Colombians. That the US is kind of pushing too hard on their sovereignty.
ParticipantB: Yeah, it seems like a lot of people on the ground just feel like they're being treated like children.
ParticipantA: Exactly! It's like we're supposed to just take orders from Washington. Do you think that's changing though?
ParticipantB: Maybe a little? I've heard people saying things are shifting, but I'm not an expert. I just do my plumbing and I watch the news.
ParticipantA: Yeah, I guess I'm just glad I can listen to people like you who have actually thought about it for years. I just have my opinions about food and tables.
ParticipantB: Hey, that's fine! Food is important. But I think the bigger picture stuff is pretty clear to me.
ParticipantA: Yeah, totally. So, do you think things will get better between the US and Latin America?
ParticipantB: I hope so. It feels like everyone is tired of the tension.
ParticipantA: Me too. It's just... stressful listening to it all day.
ParticipantB: Yeah, it is. Well, I'm off to fix a burst pipe somewhere.
ParticipantA: Oh, sorry! Okay, good luck.
ParticipantB: Thanks, you too. It was nice chatting with a stranger.
ParticipantA: You too. Bye!
ParticipantB: Bye!
